title: Best secure file transfer software: how to pick the right tool for your business
content_html:
The best secure file transfer software is the tool that matches how often your team sends files, how sensitive those files are and who receives them. For the odd file, a tool you already use may be enough. For regular exchanges of sensitive files with clients or partners, a dedicated transfer tool or a client portal fits better.

What is secure file transfer software?

Secure file transfer software sends files from one person or company to another with more control than a normal email attachment. Control means you decide who can open a file, for how long, and you can check what happened to it afterwards.

This matters to operations, finance and IT leads because files often hold contracts, payroll data, customer records or financial reports. If one of those files reaches the wrong person, the problem is yours. It does not belong to the tool.

The main options

Most teams choose from four kinds of tools. None of them is best for everyone.

OptionWho it suitsWatch out for
Email attachmentsSmall files that are not sensitive and are sent now and thenOnce a file is sent, you have no control over where it goes next
Shared links from cloud storage you already useTeams that already store their files in one place and share internallyLinks can stay open longer than planned and can be forwarded
A dedicated file transfer toolTeams that send files to outside people on a regular basisCheck where files are stored and what the vendor's terms say about your data
File exchange built into a client portal or custom softwareCompanies that swap files with the same clients again and again, as part of a fixed processTakes more work to set up than a ready-made tool

The article on why email attachments and shared links fall short for business file transfer explains the first two options in more detail.

How to choose the best secure file transfer software

Ask every vendor the same questions and compare the answers in writing.

  • Access: Who can open a file, and can you limit it to the person it was meant for?
  • Time limit: Can you set how long a file stays available, and what happens to it after that?
  • Tracking: Can you see who downloaded a file and when?
  • Storage location: Where are the files kept, and who at the vendor can reach them?
  • Your data and the law: Read the vendor's terms on what it does with your files. Ask for a processing agreement under the GDPR (the EU General Data Protection Regulation) if the files hold personal data.
  • Fit with your work: Does the tool sit next to your process, or does your team have to copy files from one place to another by hand?

If you only send a file to an outside party now and then, a ready-made tool is usually the better choice. Building something yourself makes no sense for that.

When a client portal is the better answer

Some companies do not have a file transfer problem. They have a process problem. If the same clients send the same kinds of documents every month, a separate transfer tool adds one more place to check.

In that case, file exchange can be part of a client portal that is linked to the systems you already use. The trade-offs are covered in the article on when to build a custom client portal and when to buy one off the shelf.
